Date:
December 26, 2004
Deceased: Lino Pichardo
Property :

Lot 11, Block 20, New City Block 18890, GREEN SPRING VALLEY SUBDIVISION, Unit 4, an addition to the City of San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, according to the plat recorded in Volume 9200, Page 207, Deed and Plat Records of Bexar County, Texas.
Spouse : Thelma R. Pichardo
Affiants: Karla Leticia Torres and Roslyn J. Wright
Affiants on oath swear that the following statements are true:
"Affiants make this affidavit of heirship in connection with the death and heirship of Deceased and particularly in connection with the property.

"Our names are Karla Leticia Torres and Roslyn J. Wright, and we are friends of the family and are familiar with his life and family, and knew Deceased since 2005. We are familiar with the family of Deceased and especially his children. Lino Pichardo was only married to Thelma R. Pichardo on February 3, 1966 in Topoztlan, Morelos, Mexico, and their marriage ended with his death on March 1, 2019 in San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, and had they had two (2) children, namely:

"Lino Pichardo never had any other children, in or out of wedlock other than the above, and died on March 1, 2019.

"Deceased who died on March 1, 2019, at San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, was a resident of the City of San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas, and died without leaving a will. Affiants know of no completed, pending, or contemplated administration of the estate of Deceased.
"Deceased was married only once.
"Decedent had two children, who are both still living.

"No children other than those named in this affidavit of heirship were born to Deceased, adopted by Deceased, or taken into the home of Deceased with the understanding of adoption. No children, grandchildren, or other direct descendants other than those named in this affidavit of heirship were born to, adopted by, or taken into the home of the deceased child of Deceased.
"There has been no probate administration of Deceased's estate.
To Affiants' best knowledge, information, and belief, the estate requires no administration."

"I am aware of the penalties of perjury under Federal Law, which include the execution of a false affidavit, pursuant to 18 V.S.C.S. Sec. 1621 wherein it is provided that anyone found guilty shall not be fined more than $2,000.00 or imprisoned not more than 5 years or both. I am also aware that perjury in the execution of a false affidavit is a criminal act pursuant to Sec. 37.02 of the Texas Penal Code.
